AIM Industry Partnerships · Partnerships-owned, not connected to Optimus

Non-Cert Hiring Board

Three lanes. In-field lists jobs AIM students and grads can be hired into without an A&P, tagged by nearest campus so CS can match students and flag relocation. Survival jobs lists flexible part-time work within about 25 miles of each campus so students can pay the bills while they're in school. Transferable Skills (out-field) lists entry-level technician jobs outside aircraft maintenance within about 50 miles of each campus, for grads who don't finish the A&P and students who want a backup plan. Every posting was opened and confirmed live on the pull date.

Employers on this pull with no job source in Optimus as of the pull date. Candidates for partnership outreach.

How to use this board

  • Pre-screened, not confirmed. Each job was screened against AIM's AMT in-field rubric. Confirm in-field status with Gabriela Harrington before counting a placement.
  • In-field: entry-level marks assembly, structures, interiors, avionics install, composites, paint and teardown jobs at aviation employers that are open to new hires. These count as in-field even when the rubric score is low.
  • Partner jobs are listed first in both lanes and highlighted with a PARTNER banner. The tag says where the employer is listed: Optimus, the partnerships list, or both.
  • Part-time in-field jobs carry a green PART-TIME label next to the job type. They are a good fit for students still in school; use the Part-time only filter to see just those.
  • Rubric duties shows how many of the 11 AMT rubric duties the posting describes. Six or more is a pass on the rubric. It is the test for GSE jobs and for experienced-level jobs in the other families.
  • Relo candidate means the job is more than 50 miles from the nearest AIM campus. It does not mean relocation is approved. AIM's Relocation Assistance Program covers up to $5,000 per student for a verified, placement-eligible job; the campus CS team submits the request.
  • Relo / sign-on bonus means the posting itself offers relocation help or a sign-on or pre-employment bonus.
  • Hero is an auto-flag for standout jobs: relocation offered, pay posted, multiple openings, entry-level language, or a partner account. This copy is read-only. To flag jobs for the team, use the Pick column in the Excel version.
  • Union-flagged postings mention a union, CBA or seniority bid. Entry-level slots there can fill internally before they go public.
  • In Optimus means the employer already has a job source in Optimus. This board does not feed Optimus.
  • Miles are straight-line and approximate. In-field miles are measured from the campus metro; survival-job miles from the campus itself.

Survival jobs

  • Part-time, weekend, evening or flexible jobs and paid internships within about 25 miles of a campus. Aviation-adjacent jobs (airport, FBO, ground handler, cargo, airport rental car and parking) are listed first, but any solid part-time job qualifies.
  • Schedule risk is the main screen. A first-year student who bids shifts by seniority bids last and can't protect a class block. High means the posting mentions a union, CBA or seniority bid, or the employer is a known union operation for that role. Low means the posting states flexible, student-friendly or fixed part-time hours. Unknown means the posting doesn't say.
  • Screened out: commission-only, gig/1099, MLM, degree or 2+ years required, CDL required, full-time only, supervisors, and postings older than 30 days (aviation postings up to 44 days stay, marked older posting).

Transferable Skills (out-field)

  • Entry-level technician jobs outside aircraft maintenance that use what students learn at AIM: hydraulics, pneumatics, electrical, precision measuring, inspection and documentation. Built for grads who don't finish the A&P and students who want a backup plan. Full-time and part-time, within about 50 miles of a campus.
  • Categories: airport systems (baggage, jet bridge, people mover), industrial maintenance, warehouse automation, ride maintenance, wind and power generation, field service, QC/calibration/NDT, and rail, marine, diesel and facilities.
  • Paid training means the posting offers paid training, an apprenticeship or will-train language.
  • Schedule risk High means union or seniority-bid language on the posting, or a known union craft (railroad shop crafts, elevator apprentices, utility IBEW crafts).
  • Screened out: anything needing an A&P or aircraft mechanic work (that's the in-field lane), 4-year degree, journeyman license, 3+ years, CDL A required, supervisors and engineers, and postings older than 45 days.
